title: Turn every quote request into a draft estimate by morning
one_liner: A quote form comes in, the AI checks it against your price list and drafts the estimate and cover email, and you review and send it.
steps: A customer submits your quote form or emails a request; the details land in a sheet or CRM.
The AI reads the request and your price list, then fills in line items, flags anything missing (address, scope, timing) and notes any assumptions.
It writes a short cover email and saves the estimate and email as a draft in Gmail or your CRM.
You review the numbers, adjust, and send. If details are missing, the AI drafts a clarifying question instead of guessing.
guardrail: A person approves every number and sends every estimate; the AI only prices from your written price list and never invents a rate.
tools: Tally, Typeform or Jotform, Make or n8n, Google Sheets (price list), an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), Gmail or your CRM (HubSpot, Jobber)
prompt:
You are an estimating assistant for [business name], a [type of business] in [city]. Using ONLY the price list below, draft an estimate for this request.

Price list:
[paste price list]

Customer request:
[paste form answers]

Return: 1) line items with quantity, rate and subtotal, 2) a list of missing details we must confirm, 3) any assumptions you made, 4) a friendly 90-word cover email from [owner name]. If a service is not on the price list, write 'NEEDS MANUAL PRICE' for that line instead of guessing. Do not promise dates or discounts.
verification_note: Expected: a tidy itemized draft priced only from the pasted list, explicit NEEDS MANUAL PRICE flags, a missing-details list, and a short cover email.
source_name: Make.com quote-automation guide and Zapier quote-management templates (via web search)

title: Write your monthly customer email from a few bullet notes
one_liner: Jot down what happened this month, and the AI turns it into a short, on-brand email draft that's waiting in your inbox to review and send.
steps: On the first of the month, a scheduled workflow asks you for 3-6 bullets: a recent job, an offer, a seasonal tip, a team update.
The AI turns your bullets into a short email with a subject line, a friendly body and one clear call to action.
The draft is saved in Gmail or your email platform (Mailchimp, Klaviyo) as a draft, not scheduled.
You edit, check any offer details, and send.
guardrail: Nothing is sent automatically; you confirm every offer, date and claim before the email goes to your list.
tools: Google Forms or Sheets, n8n or Make (scheduler), an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), Gmail, Mailchimp or Klaviyo
prompt:
Write a monthly customer email for [business name], a [type of business] in [city]. Voice: [warm / straightforward / playful], like a neighbor, no hype.

This month's notes:
[3-6 bullets]

Return: 3 subject line options under 50 characters, then one email body of 120-160 words with a single call to action: [book / call / reply]. Use only the facts in the notes; do not invent offers, prices, dates or customer names. End with a sign-off from [owner name].
verification_note: Expected: three short subject lines and a ~140-word email using only the supplied bullets with one CTA.
source_name: n8n and Activepieces newsletter-automation guides (via web search)
